title: Weak vs Strong Prompt
objective: Understand how prompt specificity improves AI output
instructions: 1. Show the weak prompt on screen. 2. Ask learners what is missing. 3. Build the strong prompt together using selections. 4. Discuss the difference in expected output quality.
ideal_output: Act as an executive assistant. Summarise the following note for senior leadership in 150 words. Include: background, key observations, decision points, and recommended next steps. Do not add unsupported information.
debrief_question: What specifically makes the strong prompt more likely to produce a useful output?
facilitation_note: This activity works well as a full-group demonstration before learners try individually. Keep it fast-paced.

title: Raw Note to Executive Brief
objective: Convert an unstructured note into a leadership-ready document
instructions: 1. Show the raw training attendance note. 2. Ask learners to identify what structure is missing. 3. Have them build a prompt to convert the note. 4. Compare outputs across groups.
sample_input: Attendance has been low. People are busy. We need to fix it.
ideal_output: Act as an executive assistant. Read the following situation note and prepare an executive brief for senior leadership. Include: background, key observations, root causes, decision points, recommended actions, and a follow-up timeline.
debrief_question: Which parts of the AI output would need human verification before the brief is circulated to leadership?
facilitation_note: Encourage learners to add constraints like 'do not invent causes' to see how the output changes.

title: Risk Classification Game
objective: Practise classifying AI scenarios as allowed
ideal_output: 1. Show each scenario one at a time. 2. Groups discuss and vote on classification. 3. Reveal the answer and rationale. 4. Discuss any disagreements.
debrief_question: Using AI to summarise a public government report
facilitation_note: Allowed — this is a low-risk use case. Still verify the summary for accuracy.
column11: Were there any scenarios where your group disagreed? What made those cases harder to classify?
column12: Use a show of hands or coloured cards to make voting visible in the room.

title: Prompt Building Competition
objective: Build the strongest possible prompt for a given executive task
instructions: 1. Assign each group the same executive task. 2. Groups build their prompts using the Prompt Builder. 3. Read each prompt aloud. 4. Group votes on the strongest prompt and explains why.
sample_input: Prepare a risk register for a new training programme initiative.
ideal_output: Act as a risk management advisor. Create a risk register for a new management training programme. Include: risk description, likelihood (High/Medium/Low), potential impact, mitigation recommendation, risk owner, and review frequency. Do not invent risks beyond the supplied context.
debrief_question: What was the most common missing element across the prompts your group reviewed?
facilitation_note: Award a point for each R-C-T-O-F-E element included. Announce a winner to maintain energy.

title: AI Output Review
objective: Critically evaluate an AI-generated document before approving it
instructions: 1. Share an AI-generated executive summary. 2. Learners individually mark what needs verification, correction, or removal. 3. Discuss findings as a group. 4. Build a review checklist together.
sample_input: AI-generated summary: The training programme achieved a 95% satisfaction rate across all participant groups based on comprehensive feedback analysis.
ideal_output: Review checklist: Source verification needed; satisfaction rate figure requires evidence; 'all participant groups' is unverified; 'comprehensive' is a vague qualifier; a human reviewer must confirm figures before circulation.
debrief_question: How would you build a standard review checklist for AI-assisted outputs in your own work context?
facilitation_note: Use a real-looking but obviously synthetic AI summary to make the exercise feel authentic without using real data.

title: Stakeholder Communication Draft
objective: Draft a clear formal communication for a management scenario
instructions: 1. Present the scenario: a programme deadline has been moved and participants need to be informed. 2. Learners select nudges and build the prompt. 3. Show expected output structure. 4. Debrief on tone and completeness.
sample_input: The submission deadline for the programme project has been moved from Friday to the following Monday due to a scheduling adjustment.
ideal_output: Act as a programme coordinator. Draft a formal and respectful email informing participants that the submission deadline has been extended. Include: the reason, the new deadline, any action required, and a support contact. Keep the tone professional and considerate.
debrief_question: What would make you hesitate before sending an AI-drafted email to a senior stakeholder without editing it?
facilitation_note: Encourage learners to check for tone, missing information, and whether the message is appropriately authorised.

title: Capstone Group Design
objective: Design a complete AI-enabled workflow for a management use case
instructions: 1. Each group selects a workflow from the list. 2. Groups work through: current workflow, pain points, AI steps, human review, risks, and pilot plan. 3. Each group presents a two-minute summary. 4. Debrief on the most realistic and the riskiest design.
sample_input: Workflow: Weekly programme reporting currently takes 3 hours per coordinator and produces inconsistent formats.
ideal_output: Gen AI-Enabled Workflow Plan: Current: manual data collection and formatting. Pain point: inconsistency and time cost. AI role: template standardisation and first-draft generation. Human review: coordinator checks accuracy and adds context. Risk: over-reliance if review is skipped. Pilot: four-week test with one report type.
debrief_question: Which element of your workflow design required the most discussion, and why?
facilitation_note: Encourage groups to be specific about which steps remain human-controlled. Superficial plans should be challenged during debrief.

title: Scenario Planning Exercise
objective: Generate and evaluate multiple management scenarios under uncertainty
instructions: 1. Present an ambiguous management situation. 2. Learners use the scenario planning prompt structure. 3. Groups produce three scenarios: optimistic, realistic, risk-sensitive. 4. Compare the risk-sensitive scenarios across groups.
sample_input: Situation: A new digital reporting system is being introduced across the organisation with a six-month timeline and limited training budget.
ideal_output: Three scenarios: Optimistic: adoption proceeds smoothly with peer-led training and early champions. Realistic: partial adoption with a six-month adjustment period and some resistance. Risk-sensitive: adoption delays due to technical issues and change resistance, requiring timeline extension and leadership intervention.
debrief_question: Which scenario did your group consider most likely, and what evidence would help confirm or disconfirm that assessment?
facilitation_note: Remind learners that scenario planning is not prediction — it is structured preparation for multiple possible futures.
